title: Chiliz Chain
subtitle: Layer 1 public blockchain built for sports
description: An EVM layer 1 with proof-of-staked-authority consensus and on-chain governance. I work on the Geth-based client software and the hard forks it ships.

title: Chiliz Chain Governance
subtitle: Staking and voting for CHZ holders
description: Stake CHZ on validators, track and claim rewards, and vote on chain proposals. I built the first version: the indexers, the API and the frontend. The frontend has changed a great deal since.

title: Chiliz Bridge
subtitle: Two-way bridge between Chiliz Chain and Ethereum
stack: Go, Solidity, TypeScript, Node.js, React, Docker
description: Moves CHZ between Chiliz Chain and Ethereum. I forked ChainBridge and modified it into what Chiliz runs in production, then cut its transaction fees by about 15% by moving the relayers onto EIP-1559 pricing.

title: Staking Smart Contract
subtitle: Solidity, holding over $2M of user funds
description: Sits under the redesigned Socios.com wallet, where staking unlocks reward points and voting access, and under Pepper Inc. DAO governance for $PEPPER holders. I designed and built it. No security incidents.

title: Ripasso
subtitle: Memorize anything, effortlessly
description: Ripasso is an iOS app I built for myself to keep up with memorization — vocabulary, facts, anything I want to retain long-term. It sends a notification roughly every hour during the day with something to review, picking items based on the priority I set. Built with SwiftUI, Core Data, and iCloud sync.

title: Paybitx
subtitle: Crypto payments for merchants
description: A custodial web wallet, REST API and invoice generator covering 15+ cryptocurrencies, built as a competitor to CoinPayments.net. I owned the backend: transaction monitoring and processing, invoicing, authentication and the gateway API.

title: Wenu
subtitle: Ordering made simple
description: Contactless ordering for restaurants. Scan a QR code at the table, browse the menu on your phone, order and pay from it. I built the backend and the API the mobile and web clients ran on.
